test_cases.title: Sensor and Nav Input Acceptance - Full Suite
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library with default configuration on POSIX build.
procedure: Construct a synthetic input record containing valid IMU acceleration, barometric pressure, GPS position, and nav state fields.
Submit the input record to the AFM library through its public update interface.
Read the returned status code.
Repeat the submission across at least 100 sequential synthetic samples covering pre-launch through landing.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All input submissions return JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS and the AFM library accepts every IMU, baro, GPS, and nav field without rejecting the record.

test_cases.title: Flight Phase Enumeration Set
test_cases.setup: Inspect the public AFM phase enumeration declared in the library header.
procedure: Open the AFM public header file.
Locate the flight phase enumeration type.
Enumerate every value defined in the type.
Compare the value set to {pre-launch, boost, apogee, descent, landing}.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The phase enumeration declares exactly the five values pre-launch, boost, apogee, descent, and landing, with no additional or missing values.

test_cases.title: Current Phase Output - Initial State
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library with default configuration; do not feed any sensor samples.
procedure: Call the AFM public phase getter immediately after initialization.
Read the returned phase value and status code.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The getter returns JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS and a current phase value equal to pre-launch.

test_cases.title: Current Phase Output - After Synthetic Boost
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library on POSIX; prepare a synthetic flight profile that drives the rocket from pre-launch into a sustained boost segment.
procedure: Feed pre-launch samples for at least 1 second of synthetic time.
Feed boost-profile samples (high acceleration, increasing altitude) for at least 2 seconds of synthetic time.
Call the AFM public phase getter.
Read the returned phase value.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The getter returns the boost phase after the boost profile has been applied.

test_cases.title: Phase Transition Ordering - Full Nominal Profile
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library on POSIX. Load a synthetic full-flight profile spanning pre-launch, boost, apogee, descent, and landing segments back-to-back.
procedure: Feed every sample of the synthetic profile in temporal order through the AFM update interface.
After each sample, query the current phase and append it to an in-test phase trace.
Compute the ordered sequence of distinct phase values observed across the trace.
Compare that sequence to the expected order pre-launch, boost, apogee, descent, landing.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The observed distinct phase sequence equals exactly [pre-launch, boost, apogee, descent, landing] in that order with no other transitions in between.

test_cases.title: Phase Transition Ordering - No Skipped Phases
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library on POSIX. Prepare three synthetic profiles: (a) a long pre-launch hold then immediate apogee-like input, (b) a short boost then immediate descent-like input, (c) a short descent then immediate landing-like input.
procedure: Run profile (a) through the AFM update interface and record the phase trace.
Reset the AFM and run profile (b) through the update interface and record the phase trace.
Reset the AFM and run profile (c) through the update interface and record the phase trace.
For each trace, verify that no phase advance skipped an intermediate phase in the ordering pre-launch, boost, apogee, descent, landing.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: In all three traces, every observed phase advance moves to the immediately next phase in the defined ordering; no intermediate phase is skipped.

test_cases.title: No Phase Regression Under Noisy Inputs
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library on POSIX. Prepare a synthetic profile that progresses through every phase and then injects post-event sensor noise resembling earlier phases (e.g., post-landing IMU spikes resembling boost, post-apogee acceleration resembling boost).
procedure: Feed the full nominal profile to drive the AFM into the landing phase.
Continue feeding samples that resemble earlier-phase signatures for at least 5 seconds of synthetic time.
Query the phase after every sample and record the trace.
Verify that no recorded phase value is earlier in the defined ordering than any previously recorded value.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The phase trace is monotonically non-decreasing in the order pre-launch, boost, apogee, descent, landing across the entire run.

test_cases.title: Transition Timestamp Output
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library on POSIX. Prepare a synthetic full-flight profile with sample timestamps assigned at known synthetic times for each ground-truth phase change.
procedure: Feed all samples through the AFM update interface.
After each update, query the AFM transition timestamp accessor.
Record the timestamp reported for each observed phase transition.
Verify that a timestamp is reported for each of the four transitions pre-launch->boost, boost->apogee, apogee->descent, descent->landing.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Four transition timestamps are reported, each accessor call returns JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS, and each timestamp is greater than or equal to the timestamp of the prior transition.

test_cases.title: Bounded Detection Latency - Synthetic Profile
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library on POSIX. Prepare a synthetic full-flight profile with ground-truth phase-change times annotated for each transition.
procedure: Feed all samples through the AFM update interface in temporal order.
Record the AFM-reported timestamp for each detected phase transition.
For each transition, compute the absolute difference between the AFM timestamp and the ground-truth timestamp.
Verify each absolute difference is less than or equal to 1.0 second.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All four phase transitions are detected with absolute timestamp error less than or equal to 1.0 second versus the synthetic ground truth.

test_cases.title: Bounded Detection Latency - Hardware Demonstration
test_cases.setup: FT1 flight or HIL replay of a recorded FT1 flight. Pico 2 board running the AFM application; flight log capture enabled; ground-truth phase-change times available from post-flight analysis (apogee from baro peak, boost-end from acceleration sign change, etc.).
procedure: Execute the flight (or replay the recorded flight log into the Pico 2 via HIL).
Capture the AFM phase-transition log including reported timestamps for each transition.
Perform post-flight ground-truth analysis on the recorded sensor log to determine the actual time of each phase change.
For each transition, compute the absolute difference between the AFM-reported timestamp and the ground-truth timestamp.
Plot AFM-reported phase versus time alongside the ground-truth phase trace.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every observed phase transition (pre-launch->boost, boost->apogee, apogee->descent, descent->landing) is reported by the AFM within 1.0 second of the ground-truth time.

test_cases.title: Degraded Sensor Continuation - GPS Dropout
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library on POSIX. Prepare a synthetic full-flight profile in which GPS fields are marked invalid for the entire run while IMU and baro remain valid.
procedure: Feed every sample through the AFM update interface with GPS marked invalid.
After every update, call the AFM phase getter.
Record the returned status code and phase value for every call.
Verify the trace contains the full phase sequence pre-launch through landing.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every phase getter call returns JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS, and the recorded phase trace includes pre-launch, boost, apogee, descent, and landing in order despite GPS being unavailable.

test_cases.title: Degraded Sensor Continuation - Baro Dropout
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library on POSIX. Prepare a synthetic full-flight profile in which barometric fields are marked invalid for the entire run while IMU and GPS remain valid.
procedure: Feed every sample through the AFM update interface with baro marked invalid.
After every update, call the AFM phase getter.
Record the returned status code and phase value for every call.
Verify a current phase is produced for every call.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every phase getter call returns JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS with a valid phase value from the defined enumeration; AFM does not stop producing output due to baro absence.

test_cases.title: Failure Returns Status Without Aborting Caller
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library on POSIX. Prepare invalid input scenarios: null root pointer, null output pointer, and an update call before initialization.
procedure: Invoke the AFM update API with a null root handle and capture the returned status code.
Invoke the AFM phase getter with a null output pointer and capture the returned status code.
Invoke the AFM update API on an uninitialized root and capture the returned status code.
After every error-returning call, continue executing further test code in the same process to confirm no abort occurred.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each invalid call returns a non-success JUNO_STATUS_T error code; the test process continues executing after every call without aborting, asserting, or terminating.

test_cases.title: POSIX and Pico2 Output Equivalence
test_cases.setup: Build the AFM library for both POSIX and Pico 2 targets. Prepare a fixed synthetic full-flight input log stored as a CSV. Configure a host-side test harness that can drive the same input log into a POSIX run and into a Pico 2 run via serial replay.
procedure: Run the POSIX AFM build with the input log; capture the per-sample phase output and transition timestamps to a CSV.
Run the Pico 2 AFM build over serial replay with the same input log; capture the per-sample phase output and transition timestamps to a CSV.
Compare the two CSVs sample-by-sample.
Verify equality of the per-sample phase value across all samples and equality of the four transition timestamps.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The POSIX and Pico 2 AFM phase outputs are identical sample-for-sample, and the four reported transition timestamps are equal between the two builds.

test_cases.title: Deterministic Phase Output - Repeated Runs
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library on POSIX. Prepare a fixed synthetic full-flight input sequence stored as a deterministic in-memory array.
procedure: Execute Run A: instantiate a fresh AFM root, feed the entire input sequence, and record the per-sample phase trace and the four transition timestamps.
Execute Run B: instantiate a fresh AFM root, feed the same input sequence, and record the per-sample phase trace and the four transition timestamps.
Compare the Run A and Run B phase traces sample-by-sample.
Compare the Run A and Run B transition timestamps.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Run A and Run B produce identical per-sample phase traces and identical transition timestamps.

test_cases.title: No-Regression Across Repeated Synthetic Profiles
test_cases.setup: Initialize AFM library on POSIX. Prepare a corpus of at least three distinct synthetic full-flight profiles (nominal, low-thrust, high-noise), each with annotated ground-truth transition times.
procedure: For each profile in the corpus, instantiate a fresh AFM root and feed every sample through the update interface.
Record the per-sample phase trace for the profile.
Verify the trace is monotonically non-decreasing in the defined phase ordering.
Re-run the same profile a second time on a fresh AFM root and verify the resulting trace is identical to the first run.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: For every profile, the phase trace is monotonically non-decreasing and is bit-identical between repeated runs.
